# lumis-tree-sitter

The [tree-sitter](https://crates.io/crates/tree-sitter) 0.27.1 crate with the patches
below applied, published so Lumis can ship them. Every file except
`upstream.toml`, `patches/` and `CHANGELOG.md` is generated from that release and
those patches; nothing here is edited by hand.

Use it through a renamed dependency so code keeps saying `tree_sitter`:

```toml
tree-sitter = { package = "lumis-tree-sitter", version = "…" }
```

## What differs from tree-sitter 0.27.1

### fix(lib): only match the whole name `ERROR` in `ts_language_symbol_for_name`

`patches/0001-only-match-the-whole-name-error.patch`

`ts_language_symbol_for_name` compared named lookups against "ERROR"
using the length of the name being looked up, so any prefix of "ERROR",
including the empty string, resolved to the error symbol. Queries like
`(ERR)` compiled as `(ERROR)` instead of failing with a node type error,
and `Language::id_for_node_kind("ERR", true)` returned the error symbol
instead of 0.

Backport of tree-sitter/tree-sitter@e9930e0915685efb98a9d325b8f23dfdb9e99559,
released after 0.27.1. Drop it when the pin moves past it.

### fix(wasm): copy all supertype map entries

`patches/0002-copy-all-wasm-supertype-map-entries.patch`

A parser loaded from Wasm lost supertype map entries: the entries array
was sized from the supertype count rather than from the greatest slice
end, so supertype queries matched less than the same grammar compiled
natively. Size it from the greatest slice end, independently of
supertype symbol IDs.

Backport of tree-sitter/tree-sitter@fbfb07e93de82e12784cd0f646e291b8f2e4126e
(tree-sitter/tree-sitter#6035), released after 0.27.1. Drop it when the
pin moves past it.

### feat(query): restore a query's structural analysis from a snapshot

`patches/0003-restore-query-analysis-from-a-snapshot.patch`

Almost all of `ts_query_new` is `ts_query__analyze_patterns` walking the
grammar's parse table to decide which steps are guaranteed to match, which
contain captures, and which patterns are non-local. For nvim-treesitter's
highlight queries that is 82% of a warm highlight of a small file, and it
gives the same answer every time for the same query, language and library.

`ts_query_analysis` serializes what the analysis writes: three flags per
step, one per pattern, and the repeat symbols with rootless patterns.
`ts_query_new_with_analysis` parses the query as usual and restores those
instead of computing them. The snapshot header pins the analysis code (a
fingerprint of this library's sources, generated as
`LUMIS_QUERY_ANALYSIS_FINGERPRINT`), the language's ABI, counts and symbol
names, and a hash of the query source, so a snapshot taken from anything
else is ignored and the analysis runs. A hash of the payload rejects a
snapshot damaged on disk; it detects corruption, not tampering.
`ts_query_analysis_imported` says which happened, and
`ts_query_analysis_fingerprint` exposes the fingerprint so callers can keep
snapshots from different builds apart. Integers are little-endian, so a
snapshot generated on one machine is valid on every other.

The language check covers counts and symbol names, not the parse table or
field maps, so two builds of a grammar with the same symbols share a header.
Callers that keep snapshots key them by the exact parser they came from.

Across 118 languages this took query compilation from 5.7 s to 71 ms with
byte-identical highlighting output.

### feat(wasm): load a language from a precompiled module file

`patches/0004-load-a-language-from-a-precompiled-module.patch`

`ts_wasm_store_load_language` always hands the Wasm bytes to
`wasmtime_module_new`. With Wasmtime's cache configured that is still a
SHA-256 of the module, a zstd decompression and a copy on every load:
13 ms for the C++ parser, which is most of what a warm highlight of a
small C++ file spends outside parsing.

`ts_wasm_store_load_language_precompiled` takes the compiled code from a
file `wasmtime::Engine::precompile_module` wrote instead, through
`wasmtime_module_deserialize_file`, which maps it: 0.4 ms for the same
parser. Wasmtime still rejects a file from another version or engine
configuration, so a caller can fall back to compiling. The Wasm bytes are
still passed, because the dylink section is read from them.

### Every exported C symbol is prefixed with `lumis_`

Applied last, so it covers what the patches add. `src/lumis_prefix.h` renames
284 names: every function and variable the library defines with external
linkage, plus a few static ones a macro hides from the source reader, which renaming
does not affect. The Rust bindings import them under the new names. The crate's `links` key is
`lumis-tree-sitter`, so it builds and links beside upstream `tree-sitter` instead of
being rejected by Cargo, and neither one calls the other's C code.

Wasmtime is the exception: its C API crate declares `links = "wasmtime-c-api"`, so
a project that also enables upstream's `wasm` feature resolves only when both pin
the same Wasmtime major. The pin follows the newest tree-sitter release to keep
that true.

The optional `bindgen` build dependency is removed, because bindings generated at
build time would import the unprefixed names.

Parsers are unaffected: a Wasm parser's imports and exports are matched by name
strings, not by these symbols, so the same parser loads in both libraries.
